review_type: Independent read-only review of the parent's resolved planner port
result: No new blocking correctness defect found by static review for the supported TP1/PP1, eager XPU KVarN hybrid profile. Runtime and test qualification remain the parent's responsibility. Independent-pool PP and graph/custom-builder coverage must not be inferred from this review.

nonblocking_findings.classification: Inherited unsupported-configuration limitation; not introduced by the port
nonblocking_findings.finding: Upstream projection intentionally retains global group placeholders with empty layer_names. Independent-pool classification considers the preserved spec, so an empty local group still reaches per-group byte calculation. Block-outer layouts assert bytes_per_block > 0. In layer-outer layouts an attention-empty stage can produce bytes_per_quantum == 0; an empty aligned-Mamba checkpoint set can similarly produce checkpoint_bytes == 0. The old independent allocator has the same limitation.
nonblocking_findings.scope: The active XPU V2/specdecode/prefix profile is explicitly restricted to PP1 by the platform guard, so this is not a blocker for that host candidate. Generic upstream PP tests do not qualify independent-pool PP.
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Keep the upstream projection fields and global group identity intact. Before supporting independent PP, specify zero-local-byte pool behavior and cross-rank capacity reconciliation, then cover empty attention/recurrent groups in both physical layouts. Do not restore the old local projection workaround as a purported fix.

nonblocking_findings.classification: Explicit adapter boundary and qualification limitation
nonblocking_findings.finding: Independent configurations deliberately use the module's bytes-based placement path rather than the builder's scalar block-count placement hook. A single bytes-per-block multiplier cannot represent fixed concurrent recurrent/sliding reserves plus elastic attention capacity. Upstream custom grouping remains in use, and ordinary custom placement/replanning remains untouched. Direct minimal graph profiling through the default builder is not independently qualified for these pools.
nonblocking_findings.scope: The deployed XPU KVarN recipe uses eager mode and the fork rejects its graph profile. The previous independent allocator also required fixed reserves and did not support a zero-byte graph-profiling allocation merely by setting a block override.
nonblocking_findings.recommendation: Retain the narrow adapter for this rebase. A future custom KVarN builder or graph-support effort needs a pool-aware placement contract and dedicated checks; do not treat ordinary upstream builder tests as coverage of that unsupported combination.

preserved_behaviors.evidence: The four-argument get_kv_cache_configs API, get_global_kv_cache_groups ownership, builder resolution, projection, estimate/autofit builder arguments, ordinary shared placement, ordinary rank convergence and final kv_tp_replicas assignment remain upstream-owned. The port does not restore the deleted utils planner or positional draft heuristics.

Global grouping still derives draft tags from KVCacheSpec.is_draft and gates EAGLE block-drop annotations through use_eagle_block_drop. Projection keeps is_eagle_group on empty worker projections, plus host_resident, enable_kv_transfer and role. The superseded local replace-based projection fix is absent.

Each physical pool reserves its own null block. Mamba and sliding pools reserve max_num_seqs times physical_blocks_per_request before the remaining budget goes to full-attention groups. Admission/autofit uses the same concurrent bounded-pool reserve through _independent_pool_bytes_for_requests. Full-attention allocation preserves the old least-common-multiple token quantum across differing block sizes.

Independent overrides require at least one physical block, subtract one attention null block when calculating usable attention bytes, retain bounded recurrent/sliding slots, include all per-pool null bytes and reject allocations exceeding profiled memory. The generic upstream scalar override path remains separate and unchanged.

Optional aligned recurrent checkpoints are allocated only without an override and without the independent CPU offloader, and only from spare budget after preserving one maximum-length attention request. This matches the old feature policy.

Independent workers converge each pool's block count separately and rebuild changed tensors from the actual pool count vector. The legacy num_blocks remains only the minimum compatibility scalar. Existing layout validation, interleaved block stride, padded page handling, pool_id assignment and physical pool topology checks remain.

Utils retains block/copy physical ownership, independent concurrency calculation, scheduler pool topology checks, pool capacity reporting and the shared physical-blocks-per-request helper. Planning-only policy and placement live in kv_cache_planning.

minimal_drift_assessment: The chosen adaptation is appropriately narrow: upstream's ordinary placement body is retained verbatim and independent allocation is isolated in a new helper. No additional source change is requested by this review. The local tensor helper still has an unused shared-pool mode, but removing that small inherited branch is optional cleanup rather than a rebase requirement.

performed_by_reviewer: Compared the selected planner/utils source against frozen v0.33.0 and the old final fork implementation.
Inspected new builder interfaces and engine/global-group call flow, active host recipe and XPU PP/graph guards.
Read the parent's first planning test log without executing tests or modifying the candidate.

observed_parent_log.interpretation: Observed failures were fixture migration/harness gaps: missing supports_kv_cache_grouping in local SimpleNamespace fixtures, missing mocked use_dspark in upstream EAGLE cases, and missing caplog_vllm fixture. Parent is repairing the fixtures and rerunning. This initial log is not passing validation and is not evidence to weaken production builder behavior.

not_performed: No tests against the changing candidate by this reviewer.
No Nix/native build, GPU use, service operation, model evaluation or performance measurement.
required_before_gpu_handoff: Parent's corrected planning/grouping/builder suites must pass, including local fixed reserves, physical overrides, null blocks, autofit and per-pool reconciliation coverage.
Keep independent PP, graph and custom-builder combinations outside the qualification claim unless separately implemented and checked.
